example: The peace talks became a political quagmire with no clear resolution in sight.
roots: quag (沼澤，源自古英文 cwabban 搖晃的濕地) + mire (泥沼) → 陷入難以脫身的泥濘困境

meaning: 古雅有趣的、老式而別緻的
example: The village was full of quaint little shops and cobblestone streets.
roots: 源自古法文 cointe（聰明的、優雅的），源自拉丁文 cognitus（已知的）→ 引申為別具風味的舊式優雅

example: She felt a qualm about lying to her best friend.
roots: 字源不確定，一說源自古英文 cwealm（痛苦、災禍），中世紀演變為身體或良心上突如其來的不適感

example: He was in a quandary about whether to accept the job offer or stay with his family.
roots: 字源不明，十六世紀始見於英語，可能與拉丁文 quando（何時）的訛用有關，表示令人猶豫不決的處境

example: The court moved to quash the previous ruling on procedural grounds.
roots: 源自古法文 quasser（打碎、廢除），源自拉丁文 quassare（搖碎）→ 徹底打破、使無效

example: Her voice began to quaver as she recounted the tragic events.
roots: 源自中世紀英文 quaven（顫抖），與 quake（震動）同源 → 聲音或身體不由自主地顫動

example: Troops were sent in to quell the riots downtown.
roots: 源自古英文 cwellan（殺死、消滅）→ 引申為徹底壓制、使平息

example: The querulous old man complained about everything from the weather to the service.
roots: quer- (抱怨，源自拉丁文 queri) + -ulous (充滿...的形容詞後綴) → 充滿抱怨情緒的

example: The lawyers began to quibble over the precise wording of the contract.
roots: 源自 quib（拉丁文 qui bus 的戲謔用法，指詭辯的小論點）→ 為無關緊要的細節做無謂爭論

example: The volcano has remained quiescent for over a century.
roots: qui- (安靜，源自拉丁文 quiescere 休息) + -escent (逐漸...的後綴) → 逐漸歸於平靜的狀態

example: Her performance was the quintessence of grace and precision.
roots: quint- (第五，拉丁文 quintus) + essence (本質) → 中世紀哲學認為「第五元素」是萬物最純粹的本質

example: He was the quintessential gentleman, always polite and well-dressed.
roots: 同 quintessence 字源 + -ial (形容詞後綴) → 具備事物最純粹本質的

meaning: 不切實際的、堂吉訶德式理想主義的
example: Their quixotic plan to end world hunger within a year was doomed from the start.
roots: 源自小說人物 Don Quixote（唐吉訶德）之名 + -ic (形容詞後綴) → 如唐吉訶德般空想而不切實際

example: She gave him a quizzical look when he mentioned the surprise party.
roots: quiz (考問、疑問) + -ical (形容詞後綴) → 帶著疑問神情的

example: He grew tired of the quotidian routine of his office job.
roots: 源自拉丁文 quotidianus（每日的），quot（多少）+ dies（日子）→ 每天發生、平淡無奇的

example: The senator faced rabid criticism from both sides of the aisle.
roots: 源自拉丁文 rabidus（瘋狂的），rabere（發狂）→ 引申為狂熱失控的（如狂犬病般失控）

example: As a natural raconteur, he could turn even a mundane trip to the store into a captivating tale.
roots: 源自法文 raconteur，raconter（敘述）→ 善於講述故事的人

example: The team's raillery kept spirits high even during the toughest practices.
roots: 源自法文 railler（嘲弄、取笑）→ 帶著善意的調侃言語

example: The queen appeared before the court in regal raiment of silk and gold.
roots: 源自古法文 areement，簡化自 arrayment（裝束）→ 身上所穿的服飾

meaning: 放蕩不羈的、瀟灑不羈的
example: He wore his hat at a rakish angle that suggested a carefree, mischievous personality.
roots: rake (放蕩子，指生活不檢點的男子) + -ish (形容詞後綴，具有...特質的) → 帶有放蕩子氣質的

example: The rambunctious puppy knocked over the lamp while chasing its tail.
roots: 字源不完全確定，可能是 robustious（粗野的）的變體，與 rumbustious 同源 → 形容精力旺盛、喧鬧難馴的

example: The company failed to consider the ramifications of laying off half its workforce.
roots: ramus (拉丁文，樹枝) + -fication (使...化的名詞後綴) → 如樹枝般分岔延伸出的後續效應

example: Corruption was rampant throughout the government agency.
roots: 源自古法文 ramper（爬行、直立），原指獅子等動物後腳站立的兇猛姿態 → 引申為不受控制地蔓延

example: They spent the summer renovating a ramshackle old farmhouse.
roots: 推測與 ransack（翻箱倒櫃、搜劫）演變相關 → 形容像被翻找洗劫過般凌亂破敗的建築

example: The butter had gone rancid after being left out of the fridge for a week.
roots: 源自拉丁文 rancidus（發臭的、變質的）→ 油脂類食物變質產生的臭味

example: Despite losing the election, she showed no rancor toward her opponent.
roots: 源自拉丁文 rancor（陳腐、腐臭），與 rancid 同源 → 心中積存已久、如發酵般的怨恨

example: The rancorous divorce proceedings dragged on for years.
roots: rancor + -ous (形容詞後綴，充滿...的) → 充滿深仇怨恨的

example: The insult still rankled him years after it was spoken.
roots: 源自古法文 draoncle（小蛇、潰瘍），原指傷口潰爛化膿 → 引申為怨恨在心中持續發作

example: Burglars had ransacked the house, leaving drawers overturned everywhere.
roots: 源自古諾斯語 rannsaka，rann（房子）+ saka（搜尋）→ 徹底翻找搜刮房屋

example: The rapacious developer bought up the entire block to build a shopping mall.
roots: 源自拉丁文 rapax（掠奪的），rapere（抓取、搶奪）→ 如猛禽般貪婪掠奪的

example: The rapacity of the invading army left the countryside stripped bare.
roots: 同 rapacious 字源 + -ity (名詞後綴) → 貪婪掠奪的性質

example: The two nations reached a rapprochement after decades of hostility.
roots: 源自法文 rapprochement，rapprocher（使靠近），re- (再次) + approcher (接近) → 使雙方關係重新靠近

example: The children listened with rapt attention as the storyteller began his tale.
roots: 源自拉丁文 raptus（被抓走、被攜走，rapere 的過去分詞）→ 心神彷彿被完全攫取、投入的

meaning: 稀薄的；（圈子、氛圍）少數精英的
example: Only a handful of scholars operate in the rarefied world of ancient manuscript restoration.
roots: rare (稀少的) + -fy (使...化) + -ed (形容詞後綴) → 使變得稀薄、少數精英才能觸及的

example: The senate voted to ratify the new trade agreement.
roots: rat- (拉丁文 ratus，已確定的) + -ify (使...化) → 使協議正式生效

example: The detective's solution relied on careful ratiocination rather than sudden intuition.
roots: ratio (拉丁文，理性、計算) + -cinate + -ion (名詞後綴) → 依循理性邏輯逐步推導的過程

example: He tried to rationalize his decision to quit by claiming the job was beneath him.
roots: rational (理性的) + -ize (動詞化後綴) → 為未必合理的行為尋找看似合理的解釋

example: Raucous laughter erupted from the back of the bar.
roots: 源自拉丁文 raucus（沙啞的、嘶啞的）→ 聲音粗嘎刺耳、喧鬧的

example: The hurricane ravaged the coastal town, leaving few buildings standing.
roots: 源自法文 ravager，源自拉丁文 rapere（搶奪）→ 如掠奪般大肆破壞

example: After the long hike, the campers were ravenous and devoured everything in sight.
roots: 源自古法文 ravineux，raviner（掠奪），與 ravage 同源 → 飢餓到彷彿要掠奪食物的程度

example: The old stadium was razed to make way for a new shopping complex.
roots: 源自古法文 raser（刮平），拉丁文 radere（刮、剃）→ 從根基處刮除、剷平

example: The reactionary faction fought to reverse every reform the previous government had made.
roots: re- (反、回) + action (行動) + -ary (形容詞後綴) → 對改革做出反向抵抗的

example: His rebarbative manner made it difficult for colleagues to work with him.
roots: 源自法文 rébarbatif，源自古法文 rebarber（以鬍鬚相對抗，barbe 為鬍鬚）→ 引申為態度強硬令人反感

example: She rebuffed his offer of help without a word of thanks.
roots: re- (反) + buff (源自古法文 bufe，打擊) → 以強硬態度回擊、拒絕

example: The teacher rebuked the students for talking during the exam.
roots: re- (加強) + buke (源自古法文 buschier，砍伐) → 以言語重重打擊、責備

example: The scientist rebutted the claims made in the controversial study.
roots: re- (回) + but (源自古法文 boter，頂撞、推) → 以論證回頂對方的說法

example: The defense attorney offered a strong rebuttal to the prosecution's argument.
roots: rebut + -tal (名詞後綴) → 反駁的言論或行動

meaning: 頑固不服從的、難駕馭的
example: The recalcitrant mule refused to move no matter how hard they pulled.
roots: re- (向後) + calcitrare (拉丁文，用腳跟踢) → 像動物踢腿抵抗般不服管教

example: Under pressure from the church, Galileo was forced to recant his theory.
roots: re- (收回) + cantare (拉丁文，唱、宣告) → 收回先前公開宣告的言論

example: Let me recapitulate the main points before we move to the next topic.
roots: re- (再次) + capitulum (拉丁文，小標題，源自 caput 頭) → 依重點再次條列敘述

example: The program was designed to reduce recidivism among young offenders.
roots: re- (再) + cidere (拉丁文 cadere 跌落的變體) + -ism (名詞後綴) → 一再跌回犯罪行為的傾向

example: She reciprocated his kindness by helping him move into his new apartment.
roots: 源自拉丁文 reciprocus（往復的），re- (向後) + pro- (向前) → 一來一往地回應對方

example: After the scandal, the once-famous actress became a recluse, rarely leaving her home.
roots: re- (加強) + claudere (拉丁文，關閉) → 將自己完全封閉隔絕於世的人

example: The reclusive author hadn't given an interview in over twenty years.
roots: 同 recluse 字源 + -ive (形容詞後綴) → 傾向隱居避世的

example: She recoiled in disgust at the sight of the rotting food.
roots: re- (向後) + coil (源自古法文 coillir，收集、捲起) → 身體像彈簧般向後彈開躲避

example: The victims received financial recompense for their losses.
roots: re- (回) + compensare (拉丁文，補償，源自 com- 共同 + pensare 秤量) → 以等值之物回報損失

example: It took years for the estranged brothers to reconcile.
roots: re- (再次) + conciliare (拉丁文，使聯合，源自 concilium 會議) → 使雙方再度聚合、和好

meaning: 深奧難懂的、鮮為人知的
example: The professor's lecture was so recondite that few students could follow it.
roots: re- (加強) + condere (拉丁文，隱藏、埋藏) → 隱藏得極深、非常人能理解的

example: The pilots were sent on a reconnaissance mission to assess enemy positions.
roots: 源自法文 reconnaissance，reconnaître（辨認），re- (再) + connaître (認識) → 為了解情況而事先探查

example: The failed merger led to bitter recriminations between the two companies' executives.
roots: re- (回) + criminare (拉丁文，控訴，源自 crimen 罪行) → 以指控回擊對方的指控

example: Health officials warned of a possible recrudescence of the disease after the flood.
roots: re- (再次) + crudescere (拉丁文，變得猛烈，源自 crudus 生的、未成熟的) → 潛伏後再度猛烈發作

example: The company promised to rectify the billing error immediately.
roots: rect- (拉丁文 rectus，正直的) + -ify (使...化) → 使恢復正確、端正

example: His moral rectitude earned him the respect of everyone in the community.
roots: rect- (正直的) + -itude (名詞後綴，性質、狀態) → 端正不苟的品格

example: The patient remained in a recumbent position throughout the examination.
roots: re- (向後) + cumbere (拉丁文，躺臥) → 向後躺臥的姿勢

example: She went to the countryside to recuperate after her surgery.
roots: 源自拉丁文 recuperare（重新獲得），re- (再) + capere (拿、取) → 重新取回失去的健康或體力

meaning: 編輯、刪改（文件，尤指刪除機密內容）
example: Several paragraphs of the report were redacted before it was released to the public.
roots: 源自拉丁文 redactus，red- (回) + agere (驅使、做) → 將文件重新整理、刪改後定稿

example: The kitchen was redolent of freshly baked bread.
roots: re- (加強) + olere (拉丁文，散發氣味) → 氣味濃烈到令人聯想起某事物

meaning: 令人敬畏的、強勁的（對手）
example: She was a redoubtable opponent at the negotiating table.
roots: re- (加強) + douter (古法文，懼怕，源自拉丁文 dubitare) → 令人心生敬畏懼怕的

example: The lawsuit sought to redress the damages caused by the factory's pollution.
roots: re- (再) + dresser (古法文，整理、扶正) → 使事情重新回歸公正

example: The report was full of redundant phrases that added nothing to the argument.
roots: red- (再次) + undare (拉丁文，波動、氾濫，源自 unda 波浪) → 像潮水般過量氾濫、超出所需的

meaning: 難駕馭的、頑固的；（疾病）難治的
example: The refractory patient refused to follow the doctor's orders.
roots: re- (向後) + frangere (拉丁文，打斷、折斷) → 不斷抵抗、拒絕被折服的

example: The refulgent chandelier cast a dazzling light across the ballroom.
roots: re- (加強) + fulgere (拉丁文，發光) → 光芒四射、極其耀眼的

example: The new evidence completely refuted the defendant's alibi.
roots: 源自拉丁文 refutare（擊退、反駁），re- (回) + futare (擊打) → 以證據擊退對方的論點

meaning: 使歡樂、款待（以故事、美食）
example: He regaled the guests with tales of his travels through South America.
roots: 源自法文 régaler，源自古法文 gale（歡樂）→ 以娛樂或美食使人愉悅

example: Her daily regimen includes an hour of yoga and a strict diet.
roots: 源自拉丁文 regimen（統治、指導），regere（統治、引導）→ 有系統地規範生活作息的方法

example: The artist sought to reify the abstract notion of grief through sculpture.
roots: re- (源自拉丁文 res，事物) + -fy (使...化) → 使抽象事物變得具體真實

example: The manager reiterated the importance of meeting the deadline.
roots: re- (再) + iterare (拉丁文，重複，源自 iterum 再一次) → 再三重複陳述以加強語氣

example: Her witty rejoinder left the heckler speechless.
roots: re- (回) + joindre (古法文，連接，源自拉丁文 jungere) → 緊接對方話語而做出的回應

example: The team was relegated to the lower division after a disastrous season.
roots: re- (回、離) + legare (拉丁文，派遣、委託) → 將人或事物打發到較次要的位置

example: After hours of pleading, her father finally relented and let her go to the party.
roots: re- (回) + lentus (拉丁文，柔軟的、緩慢的) → 態度逐漸鬆軟下來

example: The aging king was reluctant to relinquish control of the kingdom.
roots: re- (加強) + linquere (拉丁文，留下、離開) → 徹底放手、留下不再持有

example: She relished the opportunity to prove her critics wrong.
roots: 源自古法文 relais（殘留的美味），re- (再) + laisser (留下) → 對美好事物餘味無窮地享受

example: The old house's decor was reminiscent of a bygone era.
roots: re- (再) + minisci (拉丁文，記得) → 再次喚起記憶、令人聯想

example: It would be remiss of me not to mention the risks involved.
roots: re- (向後) + mittere (拉丁文，放、送) → 該盡的責任被鬆懈地放掉

example: Deciding on the budget falls outside the committee's remit.
roots: re- (回) + mittere (拉丁文，送、放) → 被送回、交付出去的職責範圍

example: The workers submitted a formal remonstrance against the new policy.
roots: re- (加強) + monstrare (拉丁文，展示、指出) → 強烈指出不滿的正式表達

example: Employees remonstrated with management over the sudden pay cuts.
roots: 同 remonstrance 字源 + -ate (動詞後綴) → 提出強烈的異議

example: The consultant received generous remuneration for her services.
roots: re- (回) + munerare (拉丁文，給予禮物，源自 munus 禮物、職責) → 以報酬回饋所付出的勞務

example: A cry of anguish seemed to rend the silence of the night.
roots: 源自古英文 rendan（撕裂）→ 猛烈地將某物撕開

example: The spies arranged a secret rendezvous at the old train station.
roots: 源自法文 rendez-vous（字面意為「呈現你自己」），rendre（呈現）+ vous（你）→ 依約前往會面的地點

example: The renegade officer defected to the enemy side after years of service.
roots: re- (加強) + negare (拉丁文，否認) → 徹底否認原先信仰、陣營的

example: The supplier reneged on the contract at the last minute.
roots: re- (加強) + negare (拉丁文，否認) → 事後否認先前的承諾

example: He renounced his citizenship after moving abroad permanently.
roots: re- (加強) + nuntiare (拉丁文，宣告) → 公開宣布放棄某事物

example: She is a renowned surgeon with decades of experience.
roots: re- (加強) + nomen (拉丁文，名字) → 名聲被反覆傳頌而遠播的

example: The defeated nation was forced to pay heavy reparations after the war.
roots: re- (再) + parare (拉丁文，準備、修復) → 修復所造成損害的補償行為

example: The two comedians engaged in a rapid-fire repartee that had the audience roaring.
roots: 源自法文 repartie，repartir（快速回擊）→ 靈敏機智的對答

example: The stench from the dumpster was utterly repellent.
roots: re- (向後) + pellere (拉丁文，推) → 使人想向後推開躲避的

example: The decision to cut funding had serious repercussions for the entire department.
roots: re- (再) + percutere (拉丁文，敲擊，per- 貫穿 + quatere 搖動) → 像回音般反彈延續的後續效應

example: Instead of repining over his misfortune, he set to work rebuilding his business.
roots: re- (加強) + pine (悲嘆、憔悴，源自古英文 pinian 受苦) → 長久地心懷不滿、悲嘆

example: The museum's archive is replete with rare historical documents.
roots: re- (加強) + plere (拉丁文，填滿) → 填得滿滿的、充盈的

example: After the exhausting climb, they found a moment of repose beneath the trees.
roots: re- (加強) + pausare (拉丁文，停止，源自 pausa 停頓) → 完全停下來休息安寧

example: The library serves as a repository of centuries of local history.
roots: re- (回) + ponere (拉丁文，放置) → 東西被存放收藏之處

example: His reprehensible behavior at the party embarrassed the entire family.
roots: re- (加強) + prehendere (拉丁文，抓住) → 應被抓住問責、可受譴責的

example: The condemned man received a last-minute reprieve from the governor.
roots: 源自古法文 repreuver 的轉義用法，後專指暫緩執行刑罰 → 暫時撤回原定的懲罰

example: The officer was reprimanded for failing to follow protocol.
roots: 源自法文 réprimande，源自拉丁文 reprimere（壓制，re- 回 + premere 壓）→ 以言語壓制、責備對方

example: The village suffered brutal reprisals after the uprising was crushed.
roots: 源自古法文 reprisaille，源自拉丁文 reprehendere（重新抓取）→ 以牙還牙的報復行動

example: She looked at him with a mixture of disappointment and reproach.
roots: re- (回) + prope (拉丁文，靠近) → 將對方的過錯拉近檢視並責備

example: The old reprobate had spent his entire inheritance on gambling and drink.
roots: re- (相反) + probare (拉丁文，證明、認可) → 未能通過道德檢驗、被否定的人

example: The coach reproved the players for their lack of discipline during practice.
roots: re- (回) + probare (拉丁文，證明、檢驗) → 對其行為表達否定的評判

example: The senator repudiated the extremist views attributed to him.
roots: 源自拉丁文 repudiare（拒絕、休妻），re- (回) + pudere (感到羞恥) → 因不齒而正式拒絕、斷絕關係

example: His public repudiation of the scandal did little to restore his reputation.
roots: 同 repudiate 字源 + -ion (名詞後綴) → 公開拒絕承認的行為

meaning: 令人厭惡的、格格不入的
example: The idea of cheating on the exam was repugnant to her.
roots: re- (相反) + pugnare (拉丁文，戰鬥) → 引起強烈牴觸、令人反感的

example: A valid passport is a requisite document for international travel.
roots: re- (加強) + quaerere (拉丁文，尋求) → 事先必須尋求具備的條件

meaning: 報答、回報（尤指恩情或傷害）
example: He vowed to requite her kindness a hundredfold.
roots: re- (回) + quite (源自古法文 quiter，使自由、償還) → 以對等的行為回報對方

example: The board voted to rescind the controversial policy after public outcry.
roots: re- (回) + scindere (拉丁文，切割) → 將原本訂定的規則切除、作廢

example: Despite the setbacks, she remained resolute in pursuing her goal.
roots: re- (加強) + solvere (拉丁文，鬆開、解決) → 已徹底解決猶豫、態度堅定不移

meaning: 響亮的；（勝利、失敗）徹底的
example: The proposal was met with a resounding rejection from the board.
roots: re- (再) + sonare (拉丁文，發聲) + -ing (形容詞後綴) → 聲響一再迴盪，引申為程度極其顯著的

example: The ceasefire offered a brief respite from years of fighting.
roots: 源自古法文 respit，源自拉丁文 respectus（回顧、考慮）→ 暫時停下來喘口氣的時刻

example: The cathedral was resplendent with gold and stained glass.
roots: re- (加強) + splendere (拉丁文，發光) → 光彩四射、極為耀眼的

example: The court ordered the company to make restitution to the affected families.
roots: re- (回) + statuere (拉丁文，設立、放置) → 將原本的損失或財物歸還原位

meaning: 焦躁不安的、難以控制的
example: The restive crowd grew impatient as the delay dragged on.
roots: 源自古法文 rester（停留），原指馬匹拒絕前進而焦躁 → 引申為靜不下來、躁動的

example: Paramedics worked to resuscitate the patient after his heart stopped.
roots: re- (再) + suscitare (拉丁文，喚起，源自 sub- 由下 + citare 召喚) → 重新喚起生命跡象

example: The company retaliated against the whistleblower by cutting her hours.
roots: re- (回) + talio (拉丁文，同態報復，即以牙還牙原則) → 以相同方式回擊對方

meaning: 記憶力強的、有保持力的
example: Her retentive memory allowed her to recall entire passages verbatim.
roots: re- (向後、保持) + tenere (拉丁文，握住) → 能長久握住、保持記憶的

example: His reticence about his past only fueled speculation among his colleagues.
roots: re- (加強) + tacere (拉丁文，沉默) → 傾向保持沉默的性格

meaning: 沉默寡言的、有所保留的
example: She remained reticent about the details of her diagnosis.
roots: 同 reticence 字源 + -ent (形容詞後綴) → 話少而有所保留的

example: The visiting dignitary arrived with a large retinue of aides and bodyguards.
roots: 源自古法文 retenue，retenir（保留、隨侍，源自拉丁文 retinere）→ 被留在身邊隨行的一群人

meaning: 靦腆的、不愛拋頭露面的
example: Despite his fame, the author remained a shy, retiring figure who avoided interviews.
roots: re- (向後) + tirer (古法文，拉、抽) + -ing (形容詞後綴) → 傾向向後退避、不愛出風頭的

example: "I never asked for your opinion," she retorted sharply.
roots: re- (回) + torquere (拉丁文，扭轉) → 將對方的話扭轉回擊

example: The newspaper was forced to retract its false claims about the politician.
roots: re- (回) + trahere (拉丁文，拉) → 把已說出的話拉回、收回

example: The struggling firm had to retrench its operations to survive the downturn.
roots: re- (再) + trencher (古法文，切割) → 再次削去多餘的部分以節省

example: He feared swift retribution for betraying his former partners.
roots: re- (回) + tribuere (拉丁文，給予、分配) → 將應得的懲罰分配回加害者身上

example: Critics called the new policy a retrograde step that undid decades of progress.
roots: retro- (向後) + gradi (拉丁文，行走) → 朝反方向走、退步的

example: The museum held a retrospective exhibition of the artist's fifty-year career.
roots: retro- (向後) + spicere (拉丁文，看) → 回頭審視過去的

example: The team reveled in their unexpected victory long into the night.
roots: 源自古法文 reveler（喧鬧狂歡），源自拉丁文 rebellare（造反）→ 放縱地享受、狂歡

example: The streets were filled with music and revelry during the festival.
roots: 同 revel 字源 + -ry (名詞後綴) → 狂歡熱鬧的場面

example: The explosion's sound reverberated through the entire valley.
roots: re- (再、反覆) + verberare (拉丁文，鞭打，源自 verber 鞭子) → 聲音像被反覆抽打般迴盪不絕

example: The villagers revere the old oak tree as a symbol of resilience.
roots: re- (加強) + vereri (拉丁文，敬畏) → 帶著深深敬意看待

example: The students listened to the retired general speak with quiet reverence.
roots: 同 revere 字源 + -ence (名詞後綴) → 深深敬畏的心情

example: She bowed her head in reverent silence before the memorial.
roots: 同 revere 字源 + -ent (形容詞後綴) → 懷著敬意的

example: He was pulled from his reverie by the sound of the phone ringing.
roots: 源自古法文 reverie（狂野、譫妄），源自 rever（做夢、遊蕩）→ 沉浸於幻想中忘卻現實

example: The dictator was reviled by historians for his brutal policies.
roots: re- (加強) + vil (低賤的，源自拉丁文 vilis) → 以卑劣之詞痛加辱罵

example: Her driver's license was revoked after the third violation.
roots: re- (回) + vocare (拉丁文，召喚) → 把先前給予的召回、撤銷

example: She felt a wave of revulsion at the sight of the crime scene.
roots: re- (向後) + vellere (拉丁文，拉扯) → 內心被猛然拉開、產生強烈排斥感

example: Critics were rhapsodic about the young pianist's debut performance.
roots: 源自希臘文 rhapsoidia（吟遊史詩），rhaptein（縫合）+ oide（歌曲）→ 情感激昂、如史詩吟唱般熱烈的

example: The sailors traded ribald jokes as they worked the deck.
roots: 源自古法文 ribaud（放蕩之人）→ 帶有粗俗、猥褻意味的

example: Rumors were rife throughout the office after the sudden resignation.
roots: 源自古英文 ryfe（普遍的、常見的）→ 廣泛流行、充斥各處的

meaning: 繁瑣冗長的程序、囉唆的話
example: Getting a visa involved an exhausting rigmarole of paperwork and interviews.
roots: 源自中世紀英文 ragman roll（一種文字遊戲的紙卷清單）→ 演變為冗長瑣碎的無意義過程

example: The comedy show had the audience in riotous laughter all night.
roots: riot (暴動、喧鬧) + -ous (形容詞後綴) → 充滿失控喧鬧氣氛的

example: His excuse for being late was frankly risible.
roots: 源自拉丁文 risibilis，ridere（笑）→ 引人發笑、荒謬可笑的

meaning: （言語、笑話）略帶猥褻的、大膽的
example: The comedian's risque jokes made some audience members uncomfortable.
roots: 源自法文 risqué（冒險的），risquer（冒險）→ 遊走在得體邊緣、帶點冒犯風險的

meaning: 洛可可風格的、過度繁複裝飾的
example: The palace's rococo interior was covered in gilded scrollwork and pastel murals.
roots: 源自法文 rocaille（貝殼、假山裝飾）→ 十八世紀盛行的華麗繁複裝飾風格

example: The scandal roiled the normally calm political establishment.
roots: 源自古法文 rouiller（生鏽、使混濁），源自拉丁文 robigo（鐵鏽）→ 攪動使原本平靜的變得混亂

example: The novel is a rollicking adventure story full of humor and mishap.
roots: 字源不完全確定，可能揉合 romp（嬉鬧）與 frolic（嬉戲）而成 → 形容歡快熱鬧、無拘無束的氣氛

example: His roseate predictions for the economy proved wildly optimistic.
roots: rose (玫瑰) + -ate (形容詞後綴，具...性質的) → 如玫瑰般粉紅美好，引申為過度美化、樂觀的

example: The students learned the multiplication tables by rote.
roots: 源自中世紀英文 rote，字源不確定，可能與拉丁文 rota（輪子）有關，暗示反覆循環的機械式重複

meaning: 圓胖的；（聲音）渾厚洪亮的
example: The rotund innkeeper greeted every guest with a hearty laugh.
roots: 源自拉丁文 rotundus（圓形的），rota（輪子）→ 形狀或聲音圓潤飽滿的

example: The coach's speech was enough to rouse the team from their slump.
roots: 源自獵鷹術語，指鳥類抖動羽毛準備行動 → 引申為喚起、激發行動力

meaning: 激動人心的、令人振奮的
example: The general delivered a rousing speech before the final battle.
roots: 同 rouse 字源 + -ing (形容詞後綴) → 能有效喚起熱情鬥志的

example: The home team suffered a humiliating rout, losing by forty points.
roots: 源自古法文 route（擊潰的軍隊，源自拉丁文 rupta，破碎的），rumpere（打破）→ 敵軍潰散崩潰的局面

example: As a young sailor, he roved from port to port with no fixed home.
roots: 源自中世紀英文 roven，可能與射箭術語（隨意瞄準）有關，後引申為四處漫遊

example: The essay was graded according to a detailed rubric covering clarity, evidence, and structure.
roots: 源自拉丁文 rubrica（紅色顏料，用於標示法律條文標題），ruber（紅色）→ 原指用紅字標出的規則標題，引申為分類準則

meaning: 基本的、粗淺的、未發展完全的
example: The clinic had only rudimentary medical equipment to treat the wounded.
roots: rudi- (拉丁文 rudis，未加工的) + -mentary (形容詞後綴) → 尚處於未經雕琢的初步階段

example: He gave a rueful smile when he realized he'd locked his keys in the car again.
roots: 源自古英文 hreow（悲傷、懊悔）+ -ful (充滿...的後綴) → 帶著懊悔情緒的

example: A gang of ruffians harassed shopkeepers along the waterfront.
roots: 源自義大利文 ruffiano（皮條客、惡棍），常與 rough（粗暴）聯想 → 行為粗暴野蠻之人

example: The unexpected question seemed to ruffle even the composed spokesperson.
roots: 源自中世紀低地德文 ruffelen（起皺）→ 使原本平順的表面或心情產生波動

example: The company's ruinous investment strategy led to its bankruptcy within a year.
roots: ruin (毀滅、廢墟) + -ous (形容詞後綴) → 導致毀滅性後果的

example: She spent the evening ruminating on the choices that had led her to this point.
roots: 源自拉丁文 ruminari（反芻），原指牛隻反芻咀嚼 → 引申為反覆咀嚼思考同一件事

example: The escape was merely a ruse to distract the guards.
roots: 源自古法文 ruse（詭計），ruser（躲避、耍花招）→ 用以欺瞞他人的手段

example: They chose a rustic barn as the venue for their wedding.
roots: 源自拉丁文 rusticus（鄉村的），rus（鄉間）→ 具有鄉村質樸風味的
